sections.chapter_title: Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller
sections.section_title: Programming guidelines for MII link state transitions
sections.text_helper: Section 48.9.8 "Programming guidelines for MII link state transitions" in chapter 48 (Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller), RM0522 Rev 1, page 2238.
sections.section_content:
Transmit and receive clocks are running when the link is down
Complete the following steps when the link is down while the transmit and receive clocks
are running:
1. Disable the Transmit DMA (if applicable) by clearing bit 0 (ST) of Channel 0 control
register (ETH_DMAC0CR).
2. Disable the MAC receiver by clearing RE bit of Operating mode configuration register
(ETH_MACCR).
3. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete. You can check this by reading
the appropriate bits of Tx queue 0 debug register (ETH_MTLTXQ0DR) (TRCSTS[1:0]
is not 01).
Flush the Tx FIFO for faster empty operation.
4. Disable the MAC transmitter by clearing TE bit of the Operating mode configuration
register (ETH_MACCR) Register.
5. Make sure that both Tx and Rx queues are empty (TXQSTS is set to 0 in Tx queue 0
debug register (ETH_MTLTXQ0DR) and RXQSTS[1:0] to 00 in Rx queue 0 debug
register (ETH_MTLRXQ0DR)).
6. After the link is up, read the PHY registers to identify the latest configuration and
program the MAC registers accordingly.
7. Restart the operation by starting the Tx DMA. Then enable the MAC transmitter and
receiver.
The Rx DMA does not need to be enabled: since the receiver is disabled, there are no
data in the Rx FIFO.
Transmit and receive clocks are stopped when the link is down
Complete the following steps when the link is down and the transmit and receive clocks are
stopped:
1. Disable the MAC transmitter and receiver by clearing RE and TE bits in the Operating
mode configuration register (ETH_MACCR). This does not take immediate effect as the
clocks are absent.
2. Wait till the link is up and the clocks are restored.
3. Wait until the transfer of any partial frame is complete if any was ongoing when the
Transmit/Receive clock is stopped. This can be checked by reading the Debug register
(ETH_MACDR) (all bits should be set to 0). Some old packets may still remain in the
TXFIFO as the MAC transmitter is stopped.
4. Read the PHY registers to identify the latest operating mode and program the MAC
registers accordingly.
5. Restart the MAC transmitter and receiver by setting RE and TE bits.
